problem: jobs/sync_from_erp.py connects with sqlite3.connect() and never runs PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON (off by default per connection), so DELETE FROM equipment for decommissioned rows does not cascade to depends_on and installed_in. The morning copy of plant.db has 1,322 foreign key violations (571 depends_on.src_id, 619 depends_on.dst_id, 78 installed_in.part_id, 54 installed_in.assembly_id).
fix: Run con.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON") right after connect (outside any transaction). Then, once and after a backup, DELETE from depends_on and installed_in every row whose ids are not in equipment, and confirm PRAGMA foreign_key_check returns no rows. Optionally fail the sync if foreign_key_check returns rows.

problem: The recursive step follows depends_on rows that run through deleted equipment ids, so planners see live equipment listed as 'stops if X fails' only because it depended on decommissioned equipment. On the copy, results differ from cleaned data for 817 of 2,860 equipment ids (10,527 extra rows; equipment id 238 returns 193 rows instead of 82).
fix: Fix the cause in sync and clean the orphan rows (see sync). Stopgap: join equipment on both d.src_id and d.dst_id inside the recursive step.

problem: count(*) counts depends_on rows whose src_id is a deleted equipment id as dependants, inflating and reordering the top-20 list (EQ-00252 shows 13 dependants, 11 are real; EQ-00198 should lead).
fix: Fix the cause in sync and clean the orphan rows (see sync). Stopgap: JOIN equipment s ON s.id = d.src_id.
